subject: Phase 100320: Embedded Docker Lifecycle (am compose up|down)
verdict_justification: The compose lifecycle implementation successfully delivers embedded asset materialization, OS/arch detection, Docker CLI integration, and pgvector image pinning with high unit test coverage. However, the test suite contains a high-severity defect where compose_cli_fail_tests.rs blocks indefinitely on process stdin during make check or cargo test in interactive environments, along with avoidable panics on I/O error paths and CLI formatting glitches.
standard: AGENTS.md core principles: honesty, proper completion, <=450 lines per file, accurate module headers
coverage.md gate: >=90% function and line coverage per file and aggregate
phase-100320-compose-lifecycle.md Acceptance Criteria AC-100320-01 through AC-100320-08 and test scenarios T100320-01 through T100320-12
rust-best-practices: avoid avoidable panics in production I/O boundaries
Security constraints: owner-only .env permissions and secret hygiene

issues.title: Test prompt_tty_false_is_non_interactive_and_true_reads_stdin hangs indefinitely on unclosed stdin
issues.why_it_matters: Running make check or cargo test in any interactive terminal or runner with inherited, unclosed stdin hangs indefinitely on read_line, freezing CI / local test runs.
issues.impact: Prevents automated or interactive test runs from completing without explicit </dev/null stdin redirection.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_cli_fail_tests.rs:144 calls prompt_tty(true), invoking std::io::stdin().read_line(). Task-56 running make check hung for over 6 minutes until cancelled.
issues.proposed_fix: Do not call prompt_tty(true) on process stdin in unit tests. Parameterize the reader in prompt_tty(is_tty, reader) or test read_answer with in-memory buffers.

issues.title: Avoidable panics in file backup and .env permission error paths
issues.why_it_matters: Production CLI commands should return Result rather than crashing with unhandled thread panics on filesystem errors.
issues.impact: If a user runs am compose up on a read-only directory, a full disk, or a filesystem that does not support Unix file modes (exFAT/FAT32/SMB), the command crashes with a panic.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_assets.rs:144 uses .expect("back up user-edited compose file"); crates/clio-lib/src/compose_env.rs:85 uses .expect("restrict generated .env permissions").
issues.proposed_fix: Propagate io::Error as Result<(), String> in backup_edited and restrict_owner_only, returning clear error messages if backup or permission changes fail.

issues.title: CLI help text formatting corrupted in main.rs
issues.why_it_matters: Formatting defect in primary user-facing am help output reduces CLI polish and consistency.
issues.impact: am help output has misaligned command entries (3 spaces on am compose and am retention schema) and Exit codes: stripped of indentation.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/main.rs:276-281: Exit codes: lost indent, am compose has 3 leading spaces, am retention schema has 3 leading spaces.
issues.proposed_fix: Restore 2-space command indent and 23-space description indent in print_help() in main.rs.

issues.title: Non-atomic .env file creation introduces brief world-readable window before chmod
issues.why_it_matters: Security guidelines require owner-only permissions on sensitive files. Writing then chmodding leaves a race window where other local users can open the file.
issues.impact: Other local processes or users on a multi-user machine could open .env before restrict_owner_only executes.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_env.rs:72-73: std::fs::write(&path, contents) followed by restrict_owner_only(&path).
issues.proposed_fix: Use std::fs::OpenOptions with Unix mode(0o600) to create the file atomically with mode 0600 on Unix platforms.

issues.title: Executing am compose with no subcommand produces awkward error message
issues.why_it_matters: Poor user experience when invoking the command without subcommands.
issues.impact: Users running am compose see unknown compose command ``; try am compose up|down.
issues.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_cli.rs:62-63: sub.as_str() matches empty string as other -> eprintln!("unknown compose command `{other}`; try `am compose up|down`").
issues.proposed_fix: Check if sub.is_empty() and print help with exit code 0 or return missing compose subcommand; try am compose up|down.

issues.title: Traceability table incorrectly cites NFR-6 for secret hygiene
issues.why_it_matters: Documentation traceability must cite the accurate requirement IDs per AGENTS.md rules.
issues.impact: phase-100320-compose-lifecycle.md:340 cites NFR-6 / secret hygiene, but NFR-6 in requirement.md specifies audit export completeness.
issues.evidence: requirement.md:612 defines NFR-6 as: 'All confidence, admission-score, and telemetry fields SHALL be included in any data export...'; secret masking is in §4.9.5.B, FR-29, FR-32.
issues.proposed_fix: Update Section 11 traceability to cite §4.9.5.B / FR-29 / FR-32 instead of NFR-6.

issues.title: Overstated project isolation in documentation given hardcoded compose project name
issues.why_it_matters: Users or downstream agents may assume multiple compose roots can run simultaneously without interference.
issues.impact: Because compose.yml hardcodes name: clio and .env has fixed host ports 34310-34313, running am compose down in one directory tears down containers started from another directory.
issues.evidence: phase-100320-compose-lifecycle.md:363 states running from different directories targets different roots, but compose.yml:20 hardcodes name: clio.
issues.proposed_fix: Clarify in hardware.md and phase doc that the stack uses project name clio and fixed ports, so concurrent stacks across directories require COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME / port overrides.

findings.title: Test prompt_tty_false_is_non_interactive_and_true_reads_stdin hangs indefinitely on unclosed stdin
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_cli_fail_tests.rs:144 calls prompt_tty(true), which reads from std::io::stdin().lock() and blocks during make check / cargo test unless stdin is redirected from /dev/null.
findings.requirement_ref: Test Strategy §8 / T100320-04 / Clean Test Execution
findings.recommendation: Parameterize prompt reader in prompt_tty or test prompt parsing via in-memory readers; remove direct call to prompt_tty(true) in unit test.

findings.title: Avoidable panics in file backup and .env permission error paths
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_assets.rs:144 (.expect("back up user-edited compose file")) and crates/clio-lib/src/compose_env.rs:85 (.expect("restrict generated .env permissions")) panic on expected I/O failures (disk full, read-only dirs, unsupported chmod filesystems).
findings.requirement_ref: rust-best-practices / Error handling with Result types / Section 10 Failure Handling
findings.recommendation: Return Result<(), String> from backup_edited and restrict_owner_only and propagate errors cleanly to the CLI.

findings.title: CLI help text formatting corrupted in main.rs
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/main.rs:276-281: Exit codes: indentation was stripped to 0 spaces, am compose and am retention schema were shifted to 3 spaces.
findings.recommendation: Restore uniform 2-space command indent and 23-space description indent in print_help().

findings.title: Non-atomic .env file creation introduces brief world-readable window before chmod
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_env.rs:72-73: std::fs::write(&path, contents) creates file with default umask (0644) before restrict_owner_only chmod 0600.
findings.recommendation: Use OpenOptions with Unix mode(0o600) to create .env atomically with mode 0600.

findings.title: Executing am compose with no subcommand produces awkward error message
findings.evidence: crates/clio-lib/src/compose_cli.rs:62-63: running `am compose` prints `unknown compose command ``; try `am compose up|down``.
findings.recommendation: Check if sub.is_empty() and print help with exit 0 or emit clean 'missing subcommand' message.

findings.title: Traceability table incorrectly cites NFR-6 for secret hygiene
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100320-compose-lifecycle.md:340 cites NFR-6 for secret hygiene, whereas requirement.md:612 defines NFR-6 as audit data export completeness.
findings.recommendation: Update Section 11 traceability to cite §4.9.5.B / FR-29 / FR-32 instead of NFR-6.

findings.title: Overstated project isolation in documentation given hardcoded compose project name
findings.evidence: roadmap/phase-100320-compose-lifecycle.md:363 states running from different directories targets different roots, but compose.yml:20 hardcodes name: clio.
findings.recommendation: Clarify in hardware.md and phase doc that the stack uses fixed project name clio and ports.

dismissed: Selection of single services (e.g. --services embed) activating paired profiles: dismissed because compose profiles are intentionally coarse-grained per compose.yml design.
Data volumes preserved across am compose down: dismissed because preserving volumes without an explicit -v flag is standard compose behavior and documented in §1.2.
Lack of Docker SDK: dismissed because shelling out to docker CLI is an explicit architectural decision in §2 and §5.

strengths: Clean modular decomposition across compose_assets, compose_cli, compose_docker, and compose_env.
Comprehensive coverage of happy and failure paths with stubbed Docker runners avoiding container leaks.
Precondition checks (platform detection, daemon probe) run strictly before any file writes, ensuring zero partial state.
Accurate AGENTS.md ownership headers and strict adherence to <=450 lines constraint.
regrets: Directly invoking prompt_tty(true) on process global stdin in a unit test, causing make check to freeze in interactive terminals.
Using .expect() in backup and chmod error paths rather than propagating Result errors.
Sloppy indentation formatting edits in main.rs help text.
process_changes: Never attach unit tests directly to process-global stdin or stdout streams without mock abstractions.
Always run make check in an interactive terminal before staging to catch blocking tests.
